title: Klein's "hit Remove" copy names a control that does not exist - one of the three sites is live UI
description:
1.3.0 ships user-facing copy telling people to press a button Cubric Vision does not have. Verbatim: 'paint over an object, hit Remove, and it is gone in about four seconds.' There is no Remove operation. Found 2026-08-01 while writing the docs site's 1.3.0 pages, where the same sentence had been copied into pages/vision/models.html on trust.

THREE SITES, ONE OF THEM LIVE UI: (1) js/data/modelConstants/models.js:529 - the klein-4b `description`, rendered in the Model Library detail panel. THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: it is not a changelog, it is the text a user reads while deciding whether to install Klein, and it hands them an instruction that cannot be followed. (2) js/data/releaseNotes.js:49 - RELEASE_NOTES['1.3.0'], the canonical in-app changelog every user sees. (3) docs/releases/2026-07-30-v1.3.0.md:54-55 - the archival mirror (the phrase wraps across the two lines, so a single-line grep for it misses).

VERIFIED ABSENT, NOT JUST UNFOUND: commandRegistry.js has no `remove` command (no `remove:` key). models.js itself lists `remove` under 'Deprecated (never wired to a workflow, kept so legacy history items still validate)', alongside `change`. `grep -rE "label: '(Remove|remove)'" js/` returns nothing. The only Remove labels in the codebase are 'Remove Background' (commandRegistry.js:744, MpiToolOptionsRemoveBg.js:110) - a real but unrelated BiRefNet tool that cuts the subject out. That is the trap: a user hunting for the promised 'Remove' finds Remove Background, runs it, and gets the inverse of what they wanted.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMOVES AN OBJECT: mask it with any of the four mask tools, pick `inpaint` from the operation strip, and leave the prompt EMPTY. The prompt is the router - empty runs the erase path, any text runs the fill path. This is stated correctly in the app already: commandRegistry.js inpaint.help says 'Leave the prompt EMPTY to remove the masked object', and its examples include the struck-through 'remove the tattoo' with the note 'Reads as "draw a tattoo". Use an empty prompt to erase.' So the app contradicts itself - the ? guide teaches the right thing while the model tile teaches the wrong one, and the tile is what a user reads first.

The 1.3.0 release notes also disagree with themselves: the prose says 'hit Remove' while the New Operations section in the same file lists `remove` as deprecated and never wired.

SCOPE NOTE: fixing models.js:529 is the whole of the urgent part - it is live UI and a one-line copy change. Whether to correct RELEASE_NOTES['1.3.0'] is a judgement call worth recording rather than assuming: it is a historical record of a shipped release, and editing shipped changelog entries has its own cost. The Platform Update Checklist at the bottom of docs/releases/2026-07-30-v1.3.0.md lists Patreon and Discord as unticked (though the checklist is not reliably maintained - GitHub Releases and Documentation Website are also unticked and both have happened), so check before assuming those posts are unsent; if they are, they should not repeat the claim.

DOCS SITE IS ALREADY CORRECT - no action needed there. docs.cubric.studio/vision/models/ documents the real three-step inpaint path under #klein-remove, including the 'never write an instruction to delete' warning and the note to leave the style on None for a plain erase (styles apply to the patch). Shipped in Cubric-Studio-Docs 04a400b, live and verified 2026-08-01.
acceptance: js/data/modelConstants/models.js klein-4b description no longer tells the user to hit Remove, and names the real path (Inpaint with an empty prompt)
No user-facing string anywhere in js/ instructs pressing a Remove control that does not exist - verified by grep, not by inspection of the one file
A decision is recorded either way on RELEASE_NOTES['1.3.0']: corrected, or deliberately left as a historical record of what shipped
Patreon and Discord 1.3.0 posts are checked; if not yet sent, they do not repeat the claim
Remove Background is not conflated with object removal in any copy touched by this card
